**Replay Minecraft moments exactly as they happened.**

## Overview

Recap is a Paper plugin that records gameplay on your server and replays it as a live in-world recap. It captures what players do, recreates it visually inside Minecraft, and restores the world when the replay ends.

## Features

### Players
- Movement and pathing
- Player skins
- Held items and equipment
- Jumps and interactions

### World
- Block placement and breaking
- Water, lava, and flowing fluids
- Sign text and sign edits
- Environment changes during recording

### Entities
- TNT ignition and explosions
- End crystal placement and destruction
- Entity interactions during playback

## Uses

Recap is great for creators, admins, event servers, and builders who want to review gameplay moments visually instead of relying on logs or explanations.

## Commands

- `/recap start`  
  Starts a new recording session.

- `/recap stop`  
  Stops the active recording and saves it. If a playback is active, it stops the playback and restores the world.

- `/recap play <id>`  
  Plays a saved recording in real time.

- `/recap play <id> preview`  
  Plays a saved recording in preview mode.

- `/recap list`  
  Shows all saved recordings.

- `/recap info <id>`  
  Shows details about a recording, including date, duration, world, players, and event count.

- `/recap delete <id>`  
  Deletes a saved recording.

- `/recap pause`  
  Pauses the active playback.

- `/recap resume`  
  Resumes a paused playback.

- `/recap seek <id> <timestamp>`  
  Jumps the active playback to a specific time, such as `2:30`.

- `/rc`  
  Shortcut alias for `/recap`.

## Permissions

### Record
`recap.record` lets players start and stop recordings.

### Playback
`recap.play` lets players play, pause, resume, and seek replays.

### Info
`recap.list` lets players list recordings and view recording details.

### Admin
`recap.admin` lets players delete recordings and use admin-level features.

### All
`recap.*` grants all Recap permissions.

## Summary

A Paper plugin that records player actions and replays them in-world, including movement, skins, block changes, fluids, explosions, and interactions.
